**A is still my answer.** In a lien-theory state, a mortgage by one joint tenant is only a lien on that tenant's interest and does not sever the joint tenancy, so when the borrower dies first the woman takes the whole property by survivorship, free of the bank's lien. The team note says B or C is correct, but both rest on the mortgage severing or conveying title, which is the title-theory rule, so I'm not changing my answer.

CONFIDENCE: 75
